overview.text: Christ Enthroned depicts Christ in royal glory. Hopko’s account of the iconostasis relates the glorified Christ to his coming as King and Judge, while also identifying enthroned Christ as one traditional image behind the altar.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published source; substantial verbatim reproduction is not licensed. This is an editorial summary, not the source author’s wording.

blocks.text: This medieval example depicts Christ seated centrally, blessing with one hand and holding a book with the other. Smaller sacred figures surround the throne and occupy the border. The file catalogue names the work Savior on the Throne, with a Selection of Saints.

blocks.text: Hopko places such images within the church’s proclamation of the Kingdom. His description offers several possible altar images of Christ in glory, including enthroned, transfigured and risen representations.
